safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no previous similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention whether the patient has had similar episodes before.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Prior similar reactions help risk-stratify insect-sting allergy/anaphylaxis history and can influence follow-up planning (e.g., allergy referral, epinephrine autoinjector counseling). In this encounter, urgent ED/ambulance advice was already given, so the omission is unlikely to change immediate management but may reduce documentation quality for subsequent care.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated assessment does not mention possible urticaria/hives.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not noting possible urticaria/hives can under-document a classic allergic manifestation and slightly weaken the clinical picture supporting an allergic reaction. However, the key high-risk feature (breathing difficulty after sting) was recognized and escalated appropriately, so clinical impact is limited.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript does not clearly provide full DOB including year '80'; generated DOB is more specific than available audio.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Adding an unconfirmed birth year is a demographic/identity documentation error that can contribute to administrative confusion or mis-linking records, but it does not directly change clinical interpretation of an acute anaphylaxis concern in the moment. Given the limited clinical content impact here, this is primarily administrative noise.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript does not document an explicit denial of wheeze; patient reports chest tightness but does not clearly state 'no wheeze.'
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “denies wheezing” when the patient did not clearly deny it can downplay respiratory involvement and potentially bias later clinicians toward a less severe interpretation of the reaction. While wheeze is not required for anaphylaxis and the plan already escalated to ambulance/ED, the incorrect ROS entry could still contribute to underestimation in follow-up documentation.
